title: Surgeons Are Indian Males and Speech Therapists Are White Females: Auditing Biases in Vision-Language Models for Healthcare Professionals

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the male-to-female ratio in top-k image retrievals for 33 healthcare profession prompts using the FairFace dataset and calculating Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence from an equal baseline.

Evaluating the distribution of seven racial categories (White, Black, Indian, East Asian, Southeast Asian, Middle Eastern, Latino) in top-k image retrievals for healthcare profession prompts and calculating JS divergence from a perfectly balanced baseline.
Analyzing the representation of three age groups (young, adult, old) in top-k image retrievals for healthcare roles and computing JS divergence against a uniform distribution baseline.

Examining the combined demographic outputs (gender, race, and age) in retrieved images to identify compounded societal stereotypes associated with specific healthcare roles (e.g., Black female midwives, older male hospital guards).
